response.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT d.A3 AS region, AVG(t.amount) AS avg_amt, COUNT(*) AS n FROM trans t JOIN account a ON a.account_id = t.account_id JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id GROUP BY d.A3), c AS (SELECT AVG(avg_amt) AS g FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.avg_amt) AS avg_transaction_amount, AVG(r.n) AS avg_transaction_count, AVG(r.avg_amt - c.g) AS avg_excess_over_cross_region_avg FROM r CROSS JOIN c WHERE r.avg_amt > c.g

assumptions.assumption: The cross-region average is the mean of the per-region average amounts, so each region counts equally. It is not the mean over all individual transactions.
trans.amount is used as stored (unsigned), with no sign adjustment for credits and withdrawals. All transaction types are included, including the undocumented VYBER type.

'Average each value over those regions' means the three output values are the means, across the qualifying regions, of each region's average amount, its transaction count, and its excess over the cross-region average. Nothing is rounded.
A transaction's region is the region of its account's branch (account.district_id joined to district.A3).

alternatives.interpretation: The cross-region average is the overall average amount across all individual transactions (each transaction weighted equally), not the mean of the regional averages.
